author: souptik-de
body:
pass CUPS error reason through D-Bus for frontend to display on job failure

Add error_msg output parameter to print_socket() so that the exact
CUPS error string from cupsLastErrorString() is captured on failure
and passed back to the caller. on_handle_print_socket() then includes
this string in the D-Bus error reply instead of a generic message,
allowing the frontend to display the actual reason for the failure
to the user (e.g. "job not created: Unauthorized").

Removed `fiatAmount` from the `Deal` contract's state to optimize storage slots. Now, `fiatAmount` is passed in through `Market.addDeal` and emitted as an argument in the `DealCreated` event, allowing the subgraph to index it without the data taking up storage on-chain. State variables in `Deal.sol` were also tightly packed by reducing `allowCancelUnacceptedAfter` and `allowCancelUnpaidAfter` to `uint64`. Additionally, frontend hooks were modified to dynamically read `fiatAmount` via a GraphQL query instead of via Wagmi `useReadContract`. Tests were also updated to match these adjustments.

author: giancarlosmp-hub
body:
### Motivation
- The `/clients/cnpj-lookup/:cnpj` endpoint was present in source but not reliably reachable in runtime, indicating a registration/order issue at boot rather than a missing implementation.
- The change aims to ensure the lookup route is explicitly mounted before any generic `/clients/:id` or broad CRUD matching so authenticated frontend calls stop receiving 404s. 
- The fix must avoid touching database, schema, migrations or large refactors and keep the existing lookup logic intact.

### Description
- Extracted the existing `GET /clients/cnpj-lookup/:cnpj` handler into a new dedicated router file `apps/api/src/routes/clientLookupRoutes.ts` preserving all validation, service calls and error handling. 
- Mounted the new `clientLookupRoutes` in `apps/api/src/app.ts` before the broader `crudRoutes`, for both `/` and `/api` prefixes, to guarantee route precedence. 
- Added an objective boot log in `app.ts`: `logApiEvent("INFO", "[boot] cnpj lookup route registered", ...)` to provide runtime evidence the route was registered. 
- Removed the duplicate lookup definition from `apps/api/src/routes/crudRoutes.ts` to avoid conflicts while leaving all other client CRUD handlers unchanged and without any DB/schema changes.

### Testing
- Ran `npm run build -w @salesforce-pro/api` and the build completed successfully. 
- Ran `npm run typecheck -w @salesforce-pro/api` and TypeScript typecheck completed without errors. 
- Started the built app in-process against `apps/api/dist/app.js` and issued authenticated requests to both `/clients/cnpj-lookup/123` and `/api/clients/cnpj-lookup/123`, which returned a controlled `400 INVALID_CNPJ` response (previously returned `404`), confirming the route is registered and reachable. 
- Observed the boot log `[boot] cnpj lookup route registered` in API logs during the test run, confirming runtime registration succeeded.

author: mehdi-aouadi
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Replay execution payload for Gloas state regeneration:
The state regeneration cache `CachingTaskQueue` uses soft references to cache intermediate states. In practice, the cache usually had a state very close to the target, often just 1 slot away. When only 1 block needs to be replayed, the `latestBlockHash` happens to be correct (it was set by the execution payload that ran right before that state was cached).
A bug surfaces when 2 or more blocks need to be replayed from a cached intermediate state, because the gap between block processing and execution payload processing becomes visible.

## Fixed Issue(s)
<!-- Please link to fixed issue(s) here using format: fixes #<issue number> -->
<!-- Example: "fixes #2" -->
partially fixes #10098 

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes state regeneration and spec replay paths to also process execution payload envelopes, which affects consensus-state reconstruction and could surface missing-payload edge cases (notably when older payloads aren’t available).
> 
> **Overview**
> State regeneration now **replays GLOAS execution payloads** alongside block replay so multi-block regeneration produces correct post-payload beacon states.
> 
> This threads a new `ExecutionPayloadProvider` through `StateGenerator`/`StateGenerationTask`/`AsyncChainStateGenerator`, batches payload lookups with block lookups, and updates block processing to optionally call `Spec.replayValidatedExecutionPayload`. Store-backed regeneration supplies payloads from the hot in-memory map (with a TODO noting lack of DB fallback), and tests are extended to cover PHASE0+GLOAS and validate multi-block regeneration with execution payload replay.
>

## Summary

- When hovering the pen or comment button in the selection toolbar for 500ms, a compact 26×26px popup appears directly above the button with up to 4 color swatches (first 4 highlight definitions)
- Clicking a swatch highlights the selected text in that color; comment mode also opens the comment input

## Summary
- Fixes https://github.com/ktorio/ktor/issues/5459
- `testAcceptErrorOnImmediateSocketClose`: On Linux native, closing a socket immediately before accept causes an `EINVAL` `PosixException`, which is not a subclass of `IOException`. The test now accepts both exception types, matching the pattern already used by `testAcceptErrorOnSocketClose`.
- `testAwaitClosedDoesNotDeadLock`: The server loop was not closing accepted connections, causing the listen backlog (50) to fill up when 256 rapid connections are made. On Windows native, this causes `Failed to connect` errors. The fix closes accepted connections in the server loop.
- `testMaxFrameSizeNotSupported`: The `test {}` block was incorrectly nested inside the `config {}` block, so the test assertions never executed. Moved it to be a sibling of `config {}`.

author: siomnha
body:
### Motivation

- Provide a set of small ROS2 helper nodes and pipelines to integrate `nav6d` planning with Gazebo/OctoMap and ArduPilot/MAVROS for simulation and flight-testing workflows.
- Add tools to support snapshot-based planning and future online replanning (snapshot saver, replan monitor, and reload event flow). 
- Provide TF/pose bridging, waypoint loading, and a simple MAVROS setpoint bridge so trajectory outputs can be consumed by flight stacks without implementing a full controller.
- Ship documentation and an example params file to guide users through planner margin configuration and merged-workspace blueprints.

### Description

- Updated `README.md` to reference the new `inflation_radius` guidance and linked the new docs and example params file.
- Added an example params file at `config/nav6d_planner_params.example.yaml` with recommended planner parameters (`robot_radius`, `inflation_radius`, `max_expansions`).
- Added many documentation guides under `docs/` that describe pipelines, merging strategy, TF/frame guidance, snapshot/replan analysis, and planner patch instructions.
- Added new ROS2 Python nodes under `nav6d_sim/`: `snapshot_manager`, `replan_monitor`, `mavproxy_waypoint_loader`, `tf_to_pose_bridge`, `map_world_tf_bridge`, `ardupilot_mavros_setpoint_bridge`, and `voxel_filter_optimized` with corresponding entry points added to `setup.py`.
- `snapshot_manager` periodically saves OctoMap `.bt` snapshots and publishes a reload event; it calls available octomap saver binaries as subprocesses.
- `replan_monitor` observes OctoMap/trajectory/pose/TF and publishes replan requests and reasons on `/planning/replan_request` and `/planning/replan_reason` (observe-only trigger logic with CRC/map-stale/progress checks).
- `mavproxy_waypoint_loader` parses QGC WPL or simple XYZ waypoint files and publishes `/waypoints` as `nav_msgs/Path` (transient_local QoS).
- `tf_to_pose_bridge` and `map_world_tf_bridge` provide TF->Pose and static `map->world` TF publishing utilities respectively.
- `ardupilot_mavros_setpoint_bridge` forwards trajectory `PoseStamped`/`Path` to MAVROS setpoint topic in `state` or `path` modes.
- `voxel_filter_optimized` downsamples PointCloud2 via Open3D before feeding OctoMap to reduce snapshot size and CPU costs.
- Updated `package.xml` to add runtime dependencies for `std_msgs`, `octomap_msgs`, and `sensor_msgs`.

### Testing

- No automated unit tests were added or executed as part of this change.

author: williamparis1
body:
## Summary
This PR significantly enhances the crisis communication analyzer with advanced NLP capabilities, a new FastAPI-based REST API, comprehensive logging, and improved data handling. The changes enable better threat detection through stemming, optional spaCy NER integration, and expose analysis results via HTTP endpoints.

## Key Changes

### NLP & Analysis Improvements
- **NLTK PorterStemmer integration**: Threat keyword matching now handles morphological variants (e.g., "attacking" → "attack"), improving recall
- **spaCy NER support**: Optional named entity recognition with automatic fallback to catalog-based extraction when spaCy unavailable
- **Sentiment scoring refinement**: Added special handling for "neutral-but-urgent" text (e.g., military statements with objective language but high threat content)
- **Entity gravity modulation**: Entity severity scores now dynamically adjusted by source credibility (0.5–1.5× multiplier)
- **PropagationEdge computation**: Propagation chains now include edge objects with lag, type, and confidence metrics

### REST API (New)
- **FastAPI application** (`api.py`): Exposes full analysis pipeline via HTTP
  - `GET /events` — filtered event listing with severity filtering
  - `GET /events/{id}` — single event detail
  - `GET /correlations` — market correlation results with significance filtering
  - `GET /summary` — high-level impact summary
  - `GET /propagation` — event propagation chains and edges
  - `POST /refresh` — re-run pipeline and refresh cache
- **CORS middleware**: Enables browser-based dashboard consumption
- **Lazy pipeline execution**: Analysis runs on first API request, cached thereafter

### Configuration & Keywords
- **YAML-based keyword configuration** (`keywords.yaml`): Threat keywords now externalized for easy tuning without code changes
- **Fallback mechanism**: Hard-coded defaults used if YAML missing
- **Logging configuration**: Centralized logging setup in `config.py` with file + console handlers

### Observability & Error Handling
- **Structured logging throughout**: All modules now use Python logging with appropriate levels
- **Graceful JSON parsing**: Malformed event records logged and skipped individually rather than failing entire batch
- **Correlation validation**: Insufficient data cases logged as warnings with configurable minimum point threshold (`CORRELATION_MIN_POINTS`)
- **spaCy bootstrap**: Automatic NLTK punkt tokenizer download on first import
- **Market data error handling**: File not found and JSON decode errors caught and logged

### Data & Export
- **Enhanced market data**: Sample market data expanded with more granular hourly snapshots
- **Export functionality**: Results can be exported to JSON or CSV via `--output` flag in CLI
- **Improved sample events**: Additional event records added to demonstrate propagation chains

- **Export options**: `--output {json|csv}` and `--output-path` arguments
- **Better reporting**: Propagation edge counts and significant correlation counts displayed
- **Logging integration**: Pipeline stages now log completion metrics

## Implementation Details

- **Stemming strategy**: Single-word keywords stemmed at module load time; multi-word phrases matched verbatim in original text for accuracy
- **spaCy type mapping**: GPE/LOC/ORG/PERSON/NORP labels mapped to internal entity types (country/city/organization/person)
- **Correlation statistics**: scipy.stats.pearsonr now computes both r and p-value; is_significant flag set when p < 0.05
- **Credibility multiplier formula**: `0.5 + source_credibility` centers at 1.0 when credibility=0.5
- **Sentiment blending**: 60% negativity + 40% threat language in normal case; 20% + 80% when neutral-but-urgent detected

- `scipy` — statistical correlation computation
- `pyyaml` — keyword configuration loading
- `spacy` — optional NER (gracefully degraded if unavailable)

author: maboras-rh
body:
## Summary
Automated scripts to install OpenShift Local (CRC), deploy the operator, and validate the deployment on Linux (x86_64) and macOS (arm64).
One command to go from bare metal to a running operator with validated sanity checks:



**Linux:**
`sudo bash hack/crc/setup-crc.sh /path/to/pull-secret.txt --sanity`

**macOS:**
`bash hack/crc/setup-crc.sh /path/to/pull-secret.txt --sanity`


## Scripts
| Script | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `setup-crc.sh` | All-in-one orchestrator (runs 01, 02, 03 in sequence with correct user switching) |
| `01-prep-host.sh` | System prep: libvirt, Go, kubectl, CRC install, `crc setup`, `crc start` |
| `02-deploy-operator.sh` | In-cluster operator build via OpenShift BuildConfig, Tekton install, OperatorConfig |
| `03-crc-operator-sanity.sh` | 23 health checks + optional end-to-end build test (`--sanity`) |
| `crc-cleanup.sh` | Stop/delete CRC VM. `--full` removes binary, user, home directory, cache |
## Benchmarks
| Scenario | macOS arm64 | Linux x86_64 |
|----------|-------------|--------------|
| After full cleanup | ~16 min | TBD |
| CRC already running | ~4 min | TBD |
## Key design decisions
- **In-cluster builds**: Uses OpenShift BuildConfig instead of Podman/Docker push to avoid macOS VM network isolation issues
- **Tekton CRD wait**: Polls for CRDs to exist before deploying operator (prevents crash-loop)
- **Disk auto-resize**: Detects undersized CRC VM and recreates with 90GB disk
- **Trap-based sudoers cleanup**: Temporary NOPASSWD rules are always removed, even on failure
- **Cross-platform**: Handles Linux root/developer user switching and macOS single-user flow

author: justinperkey
body:
MATCH_PATTERN, IF_LET_PATTERN, and WHILE_LET_PATTERN previously required
the symbol to appear bare after the keyword/binding. This missed the common
Rust pattern where the matched expression is a method call on a receiver
with multiple dots, e.g.:

    match self.subobject.get_result() { ... }
    if let Ok(v) = self.subobject.get_result() { ... }
    while let Some(v) = self.subobject.next() { ... }

Add the optional receiver prefix `(?:\w+(?:\.\w+)*\.)?` and CALL_SUFFIX
to all three patterns (converting them to RegExp constructors so CALL_SUFFIX
can be interpolated). Word-boundary `\b` is kept between SYMBOL and
CALL_SUFFIX to prevent false matches on longer identifiers.

Also add test coverage for single- and multi-dot receiver cases in all
affected pattern categories.

body:
## Summary

- add a curated GitHub Actions CI workflow that uses `mise` as the canonical entrypoint
- add a deterministic `mise run bootstrap-ci` task based on `npm ci`
- document the repo's CI conventions, including generator usage and v1 tool pinning

## Validation

- `mise tasks validate`
- `mise run bootstrap-ci`
- `npx prettier --check .github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `mise run ci`

---

<details>
<summary>📋 Implementation Plan</summary>

# GitHub Actions + mise CI plan

## Goal

Add GitHub Actions CI that uses **mise as the canonical tool/task entrypoint** for this repository and reliably runs the existing quality gates for **formatting, linting, typechecking, tests, and build verification** on pull requests and protected branch pushes.

## Verified current repo state

- The repo is a **Node.js 24 / TypeScript CLI** project.
- `mise.toml` already exists and defines these tasks: `bootstrap`, `clean`, `build`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `format`, `format-check`, `test`, and `ci`.
- `package.json` already defines the underlying scripts, including a composite `verify` command that runs:
  - `format:check`
  - `lint`
  - `typecheck`
  - `test`
  - `build`
- Tooling is already configured and ready for CI:
  - `eslint.config.mjs`
  - `.prettierrc.json`
  - `tsconfig.json`
  - `tsconfig.build.json`
  - `vitest.config.ts`
- There are currently **no existing GitHub Actions workflows**.
- The current `mise` bootstrap path installs dependencies and Playwright Chromium via:
  - `npm install`
  - `npx playwright install chromium`

<details>
<summary>Why this matters</summary>

The repository already has the hard part done: canonical tasks and local verification commands exist. The CI work should therefore focus on:

1. making the install path deterministic for CI,
2. wiring GitHub Actions to reuse `mise` tasks instead of duplicating logic,
3. deciding how much workflow YAML should be generated vs. hand-curated, and
4. keeping runtime/caching reasonable.

</details>

## Recommended direction

Use **`mise` as the single source of truth for tools and runnable tasks**, but **commit a curated GitHub Actions workflow** rather than relying on a generated workflow as the final source of truth.

### Recommendation in one sentence

**Use `mise generate github-action` once as a comparison scaffold or starting point, then hand-curate the checked-in workflow around this repo’s actual needs.**

## Tradeoff analysis: generated vs. hand-authored workflow

| Option | Pros | Cons | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Commit the output of `mise generate github-action` with minimal edits | Fastest path; aligned with official `mise` defaults; low YAML authoring effort | Likely too generic for repo-specific install/caching decisions; may collapse everything into a single opaque task; harder to express step-level failures, concurrency, and future branching | **Not preferred** as-is |
| Generate once, then curate the committed workflow | Gets an official baseline quickly; reduces syntax mistakes; still allows repo-specific polish | Slightly more review work; future regeneration must be deliberate instead of automatic | **Preferred** |
| Hand-author the workflow from scratch | Maximum control and clarity; easiest to reason about long-term | More up-front YAML work; easier to miss small `mise` conventions that the generator bakes in | Good fallback if the generated output is not useful |

## Key design decisions to make during implementation

### 1) Keep CI parity with local development

Use `mise` tasks in CI rather than re-encoding npm commands directly in workflow YAML. The workflow should call `mise run ...` so local and CI behavior stay aligned.

### 2) Prefer step-level visibility over a single opaque verify step

Even if `mise run ci` remains as the local “all checks” shortcut, the workflow should likely run these as **separate steps in the same job**:

- `mise run format-check`
- `mise run lint`
- `mise run typecheck`
- `mise run test`
- `mise run build`

That gives clearer GitHub logs while still avoiding duplicated command definitions.

### 3) Make the install path CI-safe and deterministic

The current bootstrap task uses `npm install`, which is convenient locally but usually less deterministic than `npm ci` in CI.

Plan for one of these approaches:

- **Preferred:** add a dedicated CI install task in `mise.toml` (for example `bootstrap-ci`) that uses `npm ci`.
- **Acceptable fallback:** keep `bootstrap`, but make it branch on `CI=true` and use `npm ci` in CI.

### 3b) Decide how strict tool reproducibility should be

The repo currently tracks broad tool versions (`node = "24"`, `python = "3"`). That is workable, but it still allows patch/minor movement over time.

Implementation should explicitly decide between:

- **Simpler v1:** keep major-version tracking and accept that tool patch versions may float.
- **Stricter v1 or follow-up:** tighten tool pins and/or commit `mise.lock` so CI tool resolution is more reproducible.

### 4) Decouple Playwright/browser setup unless tests truly need it

Today’s verified quality gates are formatting, linting, typechecking, Vitest tests, and build. The existing bootstrap also installs Chromium. That may be appropriate for future browser-driven tests, but it should be validated before making every CI run pay that cost.

Implementation should explicitly decide between:

- **Lean default:** main CI job installs Node dependencies only; browser install moves to a dedicated future UI/e2e job.
- **Broader default:** keep Chromium install in the main job only if current tests already require it.

### 5) Start with one well-structured workflow, then optimize only if needed

For the current repo size, the best first implementation is likely:

- one workflow: `ci.yml`
- one job: `quality-gates`
- separate steps for each check
- optional later split into parallel jobs if runtime becomes painful

This keeps the first version easy to debug while still producing meaningful, reviewable check output.

## Proposed implementation phases

### Phase 1 — Normalize CI entrypoints in repo config

**Files likely touched**
- `mise.toml`
- optionally `mise.lock` if the team wants stricter tool reproducibility from the start
- potentially `package.json` only if script naming needs cleanup (prefer avoiding this if `mise.toml` can stay the adapter layer)
- optionally `README.md` if local CI instructions should be documented alongside the new workflow

**Work**
1. Inspect the current `mise.toml` task definitions and keep them as the canonical interface.
2. Add or refine a CI-specific install/bootstrap task so GitHub Actions can use a deterministic install path.
3. Decide whether Playwright/Chromium installation belongs in the default CI path or in a later dedicated job/task.
4. Keep `mise run ci` as the convenience full-suite entrypoint, even if the workflow executes individual tasks as separate steps.

**Suggested target state**
- `mise run bootstrap-ci` (or equivalent) performs deterministic dependency setup.
- `mise run format-check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, and `build` remain individually runnable.
- `mise run ci` remains the umbrella command for local parity.

**Quality gate before moving on**
- Run the new install/bootstrap task locally.
- Run each individual `mise` task locally at least once.
- Confirm the sequence matches the intended CI steps.

### Phase 2 — Evaluate the `mise` generator without committing blindly

**Files/inputs**
- `mise.toml`
- generated workflow output from `mise generate github-action`

**Work**
1. Run `mise generate github-action` against the intended task path (likely the `ci` task, or compare against a per-step workflow if supported).
2. Treat the output as **reference material** first.
3. Compare generated YAML against the repo’s actual needs:
   - trigger coverage (`pull_request`, `push`, optional `workflow_dispatch`, optional `merge_group`)
   - concurrency cancellation
   - explicit permissions
   - bootstrap/install needs

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
Closes #19083

On some Windows environments, pywin32 monkey-patches `sys.stdout` with a tee writer that internally encodes via cp1252, while the outer stream still reports `encoding='utf-8'`. Rich trusts the reported encoding, renders Unicode box-drawing characters for tables, and the tee's write then raises `UnicodeEncodeError`. This crashes the deploy/serve output even though the deployment itself succeeds.

### Changes

Introduces a `get_console()` factory in `src/prefect/utilities/text.py` that wraps `sys.stdout` with a `_SafeFileWrapper`. The wrapper catches `UnicodeEncodeError` on write and re-encodes using the encoding from the exception (i.e. the codec that actually failed), with `errors='replace'`, degrading unencodable characters to `?` instead of crashing.

Replaces bare `Console()` calls in the deploy and serve code paths with `get_console()`:
- `src/prefect/deployments/runner.py` — both `adeploy()` and `deploy()`
- `src/prefect/flows.py` — `Flow.serve()`, `Flow.adeploy()`, and `_display_serve_start_message()`

### Key review points

- **Fallback uses `exc.encoding`, not the stream's declared encoding**: Since pywin32 lies about the encoding (reports `utf-8` but internally uses `cp1252`), re-encoding through the *declared* encoding would be a no-op. Using the encoding from the `UnicodeEncodeError` exception targets the actual failing codec.
- **Unconditional wrapping**: `_SafeFileWrapper` is applied on all platforms, not just Windows. The happy-path cost is a single try/except per write call. Reviewers should confirm this is acceptable vs. a platform-gated approach.
- **Protocol coverage**: The wrapper duck-types `IO[str]` (with a `cast`) rather than formally implementing it. It defines `write`, `flush`, `encoding`, `fileno`, `isatty`, `closed`, `writable`, `readable`, `seekable` and forwards everything else via `__getattr__`. Worth verifying this covers everything Rich actually touches.

author: samrat-rm
body: ## Summary This PR started as a structural refactor but grew into a full pipeline overhaul with real new capabilities alongside the modularization. **Original goal:** Restructure the codebase into a clean, extensible pipeline with no functional changes. **What actually landed:** ### Structural Refactor - Moved models, data loaders, loss functions, metrics, and evaluation into separate modules - Added `BaseModel` abstract class with decorator-based `MODEL_REGISTRY`, `loss_registry`, and `PipelineConfig` dataclass with `from_json()` - Added `pipeline/runner.py` as a clean entry point ### Hook-Based Training Architecture Introduced a `TrainingHook` extension system — the core loop never changes, features plug in as hooks (`on_batch_end`, `on_epoch_end`): - `UncertaintyHook` — tracks mean softmax entropy per epoch during training - `EntropyRegHook` — adds multi-scale entropy regularization per batch - `AttributionHook` — placeholder registered for explainability (GradCAM) ### Uncertainty Quantification Mean softmax entropy is tracked in two places intentionally — training (`UncertaintyHook`) and validation (`validate_all`), reported alongside Pixel Accuracy and mIoU. Decreasing validation uncertainty over epochs signals the model gaining confidence; sustained high values indicate the model is struggling. ### Entropy Regularization Without `EntropyRegHook`, models on imbalanced cloud datasets collapse toward the dominant class (clear sky), inflating accuracy while missing thin clouds. The entropy penalty keeps the model from defaulting to the easy answer. ### Explainability (AttributionHook) Keeps attribution logic decoupled from the training loop. Planned methods: **GradCAM++** for spatial activation maps and **DeepSHAP** for per-feature (band, DEM, weather) contribution scores. --- ## What Changed ### 1. Project Structure Reorganized the project into dedicated modules with clear responsibilities: ``` . ├── configs/ # Pipeline and training configurations ├── data/ # Dataset loaders and augmentation ├── evaluation/ # Metrics and validation logic ├── model_builder/ # Model registry and abstract base class ├── models/ # All model architectures ├── training/ # Trainer, hooks, loss registry ├── utils/ # Shared utilities └── results/ # Outputs and checkpoints ``` Split `common_metrics.py` into: - `loss.py` — loss function definitions - `validation.py` — validation loop logic - `metrics.py` — metric computation Added `__init__.py` across all modules for reliable package imports. --- ### 2. Model Registry (`model_builder/`) - `BaseModel` (ABC) — enforces a common interface on all models: - `forward()` - `from_config()` - `name` - `@register_model` decorator — register a new model with one line, no changes to core logic - `get_model(name, config)` — single entry point for model instantiation All models migrated to inherit `BaseModel`: `UnetModel`, `SegFormerModel`, `DeepLabV3Model`, `SwinUnetModel`, `SiameseUNet`, `SwinCloud`, `CDnetV2`, `HRCloudNet`, `BAM-CD` --- ### 3. Loss Registry (`training/`) - `@register_loss` decorator — mirrors the model registry pattern - `loss.py` — loss definitions - `loss_builders.py` — instantiation logic - `get_loss(name, class_counts, device)` — single entry point for loss creation --- ### 4. Hook-Based Trainer (`training/`) Introduces an extensible training architecture — new behaviors (regularization, logging, attribution) attach as hooks without touching the core training loop. **Core abstractions:** - `TrainingHook` (ABC) - `on_batch_end()` → returns optional auxiliary loss tensor - `on_epoch_end()` → handles logging and scheduling - `BaseTrainer` (ABC) — accumulates hook losses: ``` total_loss = seg_loss + sum(hook.on_batch_end()) ``` - `CloudTrainer` (concrete) — handles dataloaders, dual-encoder models, CDnetV2 auxiliary outputs, early stopping, W&B logging, seeding **Built-in hooks :** - `EntropyRegHook` — entropy-based regularization loss - `UncertaintyHook` — logs mean softmax entropy per epoch - `AttributionHook` — placeholder for Grad-CAM++ / DeepSHAP attribution --- ### 5. `EntropyRegHook` — Entropy Regularization to Mitigate Unimodal Dominance It implements multi-scale functional entropy regularization per batch, directly adopted from **Section IV of the paper**. Addresses the **unimodal dominance problem** — where a model collapses to predicting one class (e.g. always "cloudy") because it minimizes loss without learning class boundaries. Penalizes over-confident predictions by adding `-λ · H(p)` to the total loss each batch, forcing the model to maintain spread across classes throughout training. `λ` is configurable via `lambda_reg` in the config. --- ### 6. `UncertaintyHook` — Mean Entropy Uncertainty Logged Per Epoch It tracks mean softmax entropy across the full validation set after each epoch, computed inside `validate_all()` and reported alongside IoU and loss: Decreasing uncertainty over epochs indicates a model gaining confidence on unseen data. Sustained high values signal the model is struggling — a diagnostic signal beyond accuracy alone. **Mean softmax entropy is tracked in two separate places intentionally:** - **Training** (`UncertaintyHook.on_epoch_end`) — accumulates per-batch entropy during the forward pass and averages it at epoch end. Stored as `mean_uncertainty` in the training metrics dict. - **Validation** (`validate_all`) — the same computation runs inline over the full validation set and is reported on the same line as Pixel Accuracy and mIoU: --- ### 7. Pipeline Entry Point (`pipeline/`) Provides a unified entry point to construct and validate the full training pipeline with minimal setup. **Core components:** - `runner.py` - `build_pipeline(params_dict)` → wires registry, optimizer, loss functions, and hooks into a `CloudTrainer` in a single call - `smoke_test.py` - End-to-end validation script to ensure forward pass, backward pass, and hook accumulation execute correctly on CPU - Uses dummy data — no dataset or GPU required - Verified working: ``` python pipeline/smoke_test.py ``` --- ### 8. Typed Config (`configs/`) Introduces a structured and validated configuration system to replace untyped parameter dictionaries. **Core components:** - `PipelineConfig` (dataclass) - Strongly typed configuration schema - `__post_init__()` → validates: - loss name - optimizer type - learning rate - batch size - `lambda_reg` - Utility methods: - `from_json(path, key)` → loads config from JSON with: - unknown-field detection - missing-key validation - `to_dict()` → converts back to `params_dict` for compatibility with existing pipeline components --- ### 9. Dependencies Added `requirements.txt` for one-step environment setup: ```bash pip install -r requirements.txt ``` --- ## What Does NOT Change Ensures backward compatibility and stability across the existing training ecosystem. **Unaffected components:** - Data loading, validation, and metrics - Existing pipelines remain unchanged and fully operational - JSON run configurations - All current config files are fully compatible without modification - `fine_tune_models.py` - Continues to function using the deprecated `train_model()` interface - No required changes for existing fine-tuning workflows > **Pre-refactor `.pth` checkpoints load correctly into `BaseModel` wrappers via automatic key remapping — no retraining required** ✓ --- ### Backward Compatibility `train_model()` is **deprecated but retained** — still used by `fine

## Summary
- Add 155 unit tests + 5 E2E tests (160 total) achieving 84.2% instruction and 88.3% line coverage
- Harden security by fixing mass assignment, isolating dev tooling, and bounding caches
- Apply SOLID principles: remove redundant try-catch blocks, use constructor injection, move business logic to services

## Changes

### Security Fixes
- **UserRegistrationDTO**: Prevent mass assignment vulnerability in `AuthController` by accepting only whitelisted fields
- **DevSecurityConfig**: Isolate H2 Console access to `dev` profile only (was exposed in all profiles)
- **ChatController**: Bound conversation cache to 500 entries with LRU eviction to prevent memory DoS
- **RelatorioController**: Sanitize error messages returned in API responses
- **InsufficientStockException**: New custom exception with dedicated HTTP 422 handler in `GlobalRestExceptionHandler`
- **UserService**: Build `User` entity server-side only from DTO fields, never from raw request binding

### SOLID Refactoring
- Remove ~20 redundant try-catch boilerplate blocks across all service classes
- Convert `IngredienteService` from `@Autowired` field injection to constructor injection
- Move business logic (`criarComLoteInicial`, `atualizarEstoque`) from `IngredienteController` to `IngredienteService`
- Replace `ResourceNotFoundException` with `InsufficientStockException` for stock-related errors

### Performance
- Batch saves with `saveAll()` in `consumirEstoque` (FIFO inventory deduction)

### Tests (155 unit + 5 E2E = 160 total)
- **5 service test classes**: UserServiceTest (5), ProdutoServiceTest (27), VendaServiceTest (18), IngredienteServiceTest (33), RelatorioServiceTest (12)
- **8 controller test classes**: AuthController (5), Dashboard (2), Index (1), GlobalExceptionHandler (6), Produto (20), Venda (12), Ingrediente (10), Relatorio (4)
- Fix E2E test for vendas flow (modal close button selector)

author: oxygen-low
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/Oxygen-Low/LocalLLM/security/code-scanning/37](https://github.com/Oxygen-Low/LocalLLM/security/code-scanning/37)

To fix this kind of issue, ensure that untrusted input is never embedded directly into the format string (the first argument) passed to `console.log`, `console.error`, or `util.format`. Instead, use a constant format string and pass all untrusted values as separate arguments, using `%s` placeholders as needed. This way, user input is treated purely as data and cannot alter the formatting semantics.

In this specific case, the problematic code is the `console.error` call around line 991 inside the loop that migrates chat files during a username change. The first argument is a template literal that includes the user-controlled `oldUsername`. We should change this so that the first argument is a fixed string with `%s` placeholders, and `file`, `oldUsername`, and `migrationErr` are passed as subsequent arguments. For example, change:

```js
console.error(`Change-username: failed to re-encrypt chat file ${file} for ${oldUsername}:`, migrationErr);
```

to:

```js
console.error('Change-username: failed to re-encrypt chat file %s for %s:', file, oldUsername, migrationErr);
```

This preserves the same information content in the log and keeps `migrationErr` as a separate argument, while ensuring the format string itself cannot be influenced by user input. No new imports or dependencies are needed, and no other parts of the file need to change.

author: luckypipewrench
body:
## Summary

- Three-layer unprivileged process containment for agent subprocesses: Landlock filesystem restriction, seccomp BPF syscall filter, and network namespace isolation
- Re-exec launcher pattern keeps pipelock unrestricted while the child is fully contained
- Two modes: `--sandbox` on `mcp proxy` (MCP stdio) and `pipelock sandbox -- COMMAND` (standalone with bridge proxy)
- Argument-level seccomp filtering blocks clone CLONE_NEW* flags, AF_VSOCK sockets, and restricts personality values
- Per-sandbox /tmp scoping prevents cross-sandbox temp file leakage
- Synthetic environment allowlist prevents secret leakage; dangerous env keys (LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS) blocked from --env passthrough
- Resource limits (NPROC, NOFILE, FSIZE, CORE) constrain child resource consumption
- Best-effort degradation: each layer applied independently, clear reporting of active/missing layers
- New dependency: go-landlock v0.7.0 (official Landlock Go bindings)
- 130 tests including subprocess integration tests verifying kernel enforcement

### Known limitations

- **/dev/shm:** Allowed read-write for Python multiprocessing and Chromium compatibility. Same-user shared memory segments remain reachable from inside the sandbox. Planned fix: private tmpfs mount in strict mode.
- **clone3 CLONE_NEW\*:** BPF cannot dereference clone3's pointer argument to inspect flags. Mitigated by: Landlock restrictions survive namespace creation, mount is blocked by seccomp, no_new_privs prevents suid escalation.
- **Detached descendants:** Grandchildren that call setsid() escape process group cleanup. Standalone mode uses a 5s drain timeout. Planned fix: PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER in strict mode.

  - Added a Linux-only sandbox mode: new sandbox CLI, optional --sandbox proxy mode, workspace & filesystem policy, capability probing, containment layers (Landlock, seccomp, rlimits), synthetic sandbox environment, and a standalone bridge/proxy flow for sandboxed agents.
* **Tests**
  - Large suite of unit and integration tests covering init paths, landlock/rlimit/seccomp, launcher/bridge, env handling, and proxy sandboxing.

  - Updated coverage exclusions and module/dependency declarations.

author: shyam-repeat
body:
### Motivation
- The quiz overlay was overflowing on smaller screens and the train Rive graphic could become too large to fit the inlaid quiz area. The floating mascot also intruded on the main card area making the UI look cluttered.
- The overlay could appear even when the app that triggered the quiz was no longer in the foreground, causing confusing behavior and stale overlays.

### Description
- Make the inlaid overlay area a full white modern surface by moving the outer 20dp inset to the service and rendering the full quiz surface as white in `QuizCardRouter` so train + quiz content share the full area cleanly and the mascot is removed from the quiz card area (`app/src/main/java/.../QuizCardRouter.kt`).
- Update `TrainAnimation` to auto-fit: compute a scale using both width and height (`min(widthScale, heightScale)`) and adjust entry/bounce transforms so the train reliably stays on screen at smaller sizes (`app/src/main/java/.../TrainAnimation.kt`).
- Simplify `ModernQuizBackground` to keep subtle accent shapes but render the inlaid background white and allow the `20.dp` outer padding to remain in the service layer (`app/src/main/java/.../ModernQuizBackground.kt`).
- Enforce foreground-app behavior in the overlay service by recording the source app that triggered the overlay, refusing to show the overlay if that app is not currently foreground, and removing the overlay when that source app is backgrounded (`app/src/main/java/.../OverlayForegroundService.kt`).
- Misc: cleaned up related imports and removed redundant mascot placement within the overlay card to prevent layout overlap.

### Testing
- Attempted to run a Kotlin compilation with Gradle: `./gradlew --no-daemon :app:compileDebugKotlin`, which failed in this environment because the Android SDK is not configured (missing `ANDROID_HOME` / `local.properties` `sdk.dir`).
- Code changes were committed locally with the message `Fix quiz overlay sizing and foreground behavior` and the modified files were validated with `git diff`/`git status` in the working tree.

author: allanmaldonado
body:
1. `DoacaoController` recebe a requisição de cadastro.
2. `DoacaoService` valida os dados básicos e aplica a validação por strategy.
3. A doação é persistida no `DoacaoDAL`.
4. Após persistir com sucesso, `DoacaoService` chama `DoacaoEventPublisher.publicar(doacaoSalva)`.
5. O publisher notifica todos os observers registrados via interface `DoacaoObserver`.
6. Cada observer executa sua responsabilidade isoladamente:
   - `LogDoacaoObserver`: registra informações da doação
   - `ContadorDoacaoObserver`: incrementa o contador em memória

author: copilot
body:
`DiscoverySessionRow` declared its session as a plain `let`, so SwiftUI never subscribed to `@Published` changes — the timer and path list were frozen on first render. Compounding this, SwiftUI tears down `DiscoverySessionRow` on tab switch, so returning to the tab showed a stale, permanently-frozen state.

## Changes

### `AppProtection.swift`
- Added `Identifiable` conformance to `DiscoverySession` (`let id = UUID()`) to support `.sheet(item:)`

### `PresetsView.swift`
- `DiscoverySessionRow.session`: `let` → `@ObservedObject var` — subscribes to `timeRemaining`, `capturedPaths`, `isComplete` changes
- Removed `private` from `DiscoverySessionRow` (now referenced from `ContentView`)
- Removed the inline session `Section` from `PresetsView` — presentation moved to a modal

### `ContentView.swift`
- Added `@StateObject private var protectionStore = AppProtectionStore.shared`
- Added a top-level `.sheet(item:)` bound to `protectionStore.activeDiscovery`

```swift
// The binding setter is intentionally a no-op: interactive dismissal is disabled,
// and the sheet is dismissed only by the Cancel/Finalize actions in DiscoverySessionRow,
// which call AppProtectionStore.shared.cancelDiscovery() or finalizeDiscovery(_:for:).
.sheet(item: Binding(get: { protectionStore.activeDiscovery }, set: { _ in })) { session in
    DiscoverySessionRow(session: session)
        .padding()
        .frame(minWidth: 500)
        .interactiveDismissDisabled()
}
```

Anchoring the sheet at `ContentView` means the session view is never torn down by tab navigation. `AppProtectionStore.forwardDiscoveryChanges()` already forwarded `objectWillChange` from the session through the store, so `PresetsView` re-renders correctly when `activeDiscovery` is set/cleared.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>DiscoverySession: realtime path updates broken, timer freezes on tab switch — move to modal popover</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Summary
> 
> The App Protections discovery session has three related bugs, all rooted in how the SwiftUI view observes the session object. The fix also warrants a UX change: moving the session into a modal popover so it lives independently of the tab hierarchy.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Bug 1 — `DiscoverySessionRow` never re-renders when paths or the timer change
> 
> `DiscoverySessionRow` declares its session as a plain `let`:
> 
> ```swift
> private struct DiscoverySessionRow: View {
>     let session: DiscoverySession  // ← not @ObservedObject
> ```
> 
> `DiscoverySession` is an `ObservableObject` with `@Published` properties (`timeRemaining`, `capturedPaths`, `isComplete`), but because the row doesn't declare `@ObservedObject`, SwiftUI never subscribes to those change notifications. The timer badge reads `session.timeRemaining` and the path list reads `session.capturedPaths`, but neither will ever re-render after initial display.
> 
> **Fix:** change the declaration to `@ObservedObject var session: DiscoverySession`.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Bug 2 — Path updates from opfilter events don't surface in the parent view
> 
> Even if Bug 1 is fixed, `PresetsView` passes the session down as a value derived from `protectionStore.activeDiscovery`. `PresetsView` observes `protectionStore` (an `AppProtectionStore`), not the session itself. When `DiscoverySession.capturedPaths` fires `objectWillChange`, only subscribers of the session hear it — `PresetsView` doesn't re-render because `AppProtectionStore` doesn't re-publish the session's changes.
> 
> **Fix:** either forward the session's `objectWillChange` through `AppProtectionStore` (e.g. store a `Cancellable` that calls `objectWillChange.send()` whenever the session fires), or rely solely on `@ObservedObject` in `DiscoverySessionRow` to drive updates (which works once Bug 1 is fixed, since the row owns the observation directly).
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Bug 3 — Timer appears frozen after switching tabs and returning
> 
> When the user navigates away from the App Protections tab and back, SwiftUI tears down and recreates `DiscoverySessionRow`. The underlying `DiscoverySession` object is still alive and its timer is still running (it lives on `AppProtectionStore`), but the new `DiscoverySessionRow` struct is a fresh instance with a plain `let` — it was never observing and still isn't. The countdown badge shows a stale value and never ticks.
> 
> This is a symptom of Bug 1, but the tab-switch makes it visually obvious: the timer jumps to a stale number on re-entry and then freezes.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Proposed fix — modal popover for the whole session
> 
> Rather than embedding the session inline in the list (where it is subject to SwiftUI's view lifecycle tied to navigation), present it as a persistent modal sheet or popover anchored to the main window. This means:
> 
> - The session view is never torn down while the session is active, regardless of which tab the user is on.
> - The countdown and captured paths update in real time without fighting SwiftUI's navigation lifecycle.
> - It makes the in-progress state more visible and harder to accidentally dismiss by switching tabs.
> - Cancelling or completing the session dismisses the popover naturally.
> 
> A `.sheet(isPresented:)` driven by `AppProtectionStore.activeDiscovery != nil` at the top-level window view would achieve this with minimal structural change.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Acceptance criteria
> 
> - [ ] Captured paths appear in real time as opfilter events arrive during a session.
> - [ ] The countdown timer ticks every second without interruption.
> - [ ] Switching to another tab and back does not freeze the timer or lose captured paths.
> - [ ] The session is presented as a modal that persists across tab changes.
> - [ ] Cancelling or completing the session dismisses the modal.</issue_description>
>

author: puma7
body:
## Summary

Adds a new `KiaHyundaiToken/` folder alongside the existing `Hyundai Token Solution/` with a standalone tool for retrieving OAuth2 refresh tokens via browser login.

### Key differences from the existing Hyundai Token Solution

- **Kia + Hyundai support** — works with both brands (existing solution is Hyundai-only)
- **Multi-region** — Europe, China, Australia, New Zealand, India, Brazil
- **Automatic ChromeDriver** — detects installed Chrome version and downloads the matching driver automatically, no manual setup
- **Anti-detection flags** — uses stealth browser options to avoid bot detection and reCAPTCHA issues
- **Single script** — one `get_token.py` with interactive region/brand selection

### Files added

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `KiaHyundaiToken/get_token.py` | Main token retrieval script |
| `KiaHyundaiToken/requirements.txt` | Python dependencies (selenium, requests, chromedriver-autoinstaller) |
| `KiaHyundaiToken/README.md` | Setup guide, usage instructions, and troubleshooting |

### Supported regions

| Region | Kia | Hyundai | Status |
|--------|-----|---------|--------|
| Europe | ✅ | ✅ | Kia confirmed, Hyundai experimental |
| China | ✅ | ✅ | untested |
| Australia | ✅ | ✅ | untested |
| New Zealand | ✅ | — | untested |
| India | ✅ | ✅ | untested |
| Brazil | — | ✅ | untested |

### How it works

1. User selects region and brand
2. Script opens Chrome with the OAuth login page
3. User logs in manually (solving any CAPTCHA)
4. Script intercepts the authorization code and exchanges it for a refresh token
5. Refresh token is displayed — can be used as password in Home Assistant

### Why a separate folder?

The existing `Hyundai Token Solution/` focuses on Hyundai-only with manual ChromeDriver setup. This solution takes a different approach (multi-brand, auto-setup), so it lives in its own folder to avoid breaking the existing workflow.

body:
## Summary
Reorganized the type system by splitting the large `src/core/types/domain.ts` file (1335 lines) into focused, domain-specific modules. This improves code organization, maintainability, and makes dependencies clearer.

## Key Changes

- **Created new type modules:**
  - `common.ts` - Shared types (SkillTag, Artifact, ArtifactTags, Ladder, Rung, MilestoneProgress)
  - `family.ts` - Family and child management (FamilySettings, Child)
  - `planning.ts` - Planning and daily logging (WeekPlan, DayLog, DayBlock, ChecklistItem, Session, DailyPlan, etc.)
  - `compliance.ts` - Hours tracking and adjustments (HoursEntry, HoursAdjustment)
  - `evaluation.ts` - Evaluation and skill assessment (Evaluation, PrioritySkill, SkillSnapshot, etc.)
  - `dadlab.ts` - Project and lab session management (Project, LabSession, SessionLogEntry, DadLabReport, ChildLabReport)
  - `books.ts` - Book builder types (Book, BookPage, BookTheme, StickerTag, SightWordProgress)
  - `xp.ts` - XP and avatar system (XpLedger, ArmorPiece, AvatarProfile, DailyArmorSession)
  - `index.ts` - Central re-export point for all types

- **Updated all imports** across 100+ files to use the new modular structure:
  - Changed from `'../../core/types/domain'` to `'../../core/types'` (via index.ts re-exports)
  - Specific imports now reference the appropriate module (e.g., `'../../core/types/planning'`)

- **Preserved all type definitions** - No breaking changes to the actual type interfaces, only reorganization

## Benefits

- **Better separation of concerns** - Types are grouped by domain/feature
- **Clearer dependencies** - Easier to see what each module depends on
- **Improved maintainability** - Smaller files are easier to navigate and modify
- **Scalability** - New features can add their own type modules without bloating existing files
- **Backward compatibility** - Central index.ts allows gradual migration of imports

author: copilot
body:
The dashboard lacked any live simulation controls — data loaded once on mount with no way to pause, reset, or vary refresh rate.

## New components

- **`SimulationControls.jsx`** — Play / Pause / Stop / Reset buttons + 0.5x/1x/2x/4x speed dropdown. Button enable/disable states follow the spec:

  | State | Play | Pause | Stop | Speed |
  |-------|------|-------|------|-------|
  | Running | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
  | Paused | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
  | Stopped | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |

- **`SimulationStatusBar.jsx`** — Status pill (Running / Paused / Stopped), elapsed simulated time as `Day X, HH:MM UTC`, and speed badge.

## App.js — simulation state & interval

Added `isSimulationRunning`, `isSimulationPaused`, `simulationSpeed`, `elapsedSimulationTime` state. A `setInterval` effect drives periodic refresh:

```js
const intervalMs = Math.round(5000 / simulationSpeed);
simulationIntervalRef.current = setInterval(() => {
  refreshStreamData(activeStream);
  setElapsedSimulationTime(prev => prev + 5000); // each cycle = 5 s simulated
}, intervalMs);
```

Elapsed time increments by a fixed 5 000 ms per cycle regardless of speed, so at 2x (interval = 2 500 ms) two cycles fire per 5 real seconds → 10 s simulated, giving a true speed multiplier effect on the clock display.

**Stop** clears all data, alarms, and KPIs to zero (status set to a zeroed placeholder to avoid null crashes). **Reset** regenerates fresh data and restarts at 1x.

## Integration

- `DashboardPage.jsx` — extended props to forward simulation state + handlers.
- `StatusHeader.jsx` — renders `SimulationStatusBar` (left) and `SimulationControls` (right) alongside existing pills and icon buttons.
- `App.css` — styles for both new components with per-state colour coding (green play, yellow pause, red stop, teal reset) and responsive stacking below 620 px.

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Overview
Add comprehensive simulation control features to the Hospital Oxygen Dashboard to give users better control over the simulated data generation and monitoring experience.

## Features to Implement

### 1. Play/Pause/Stop Simulation Controls
- **Play Button**: Resume simulation from paused state
- **Pause Button**: Halt real-time data updates while preserving current state and data
- **Stop Button**: Completely reset simulation (clears all data and alarms)

### 2. Simulation Speed Control
- Implement 4 preset speed options: **0.5x, 1x, 2x, 4x**
- Speed multiplier affects the data refresh rate dynamically
  - 0.5x speed: 10-second refresh interval
  - 1x speed: 5-second refresh interval (default)
  - 2x speed: 2.5-second refresh interval
  - 4x speed: 1.25-second refresh interval
- Allow speed changes while simulation is running
- Display current speed in status bar

### 3. Simulation Reset Button
- Clears all historical data
- Resets all alarms to acknowledged/cleared state
- Regenerates fresh simulation data with new random values
- Restarts automatically with 1x speed

### 4. Elapsed Time Display
- Show simulated time progression (not real wall-clock time)
- Format: "Day X, HH:MM UTC"
- Updates with each simulation cycle
- Display in status bar

## Technical Requirements

### State Management
Track the following simulation states in App.js:
- `isSimulationRunning`: Boolean indicating if simulation is active
- `isSimulationPaused`: Boolean indicating if simulation is paused
- `simulationSpeed`: Current speed multiplier (0.5, 1, 2, or 4)
- `simulationStartTime`: Timestamp when simulation began
- `elapsedSimulationTime`: Total elapsed simulated milliseconds

### Components to Create/Modify

1. **New Component: SimulationControls.js**
   - Display Play, Pause, Stop buttons
   - Display Speed selector dropdown (0.5x, 1x, 2x, 4x)
   - Disable/enable buttons based on simulation state
   - Responsive design matching current dashboard style

2. **New Component: SimulationStatusBar.js**
   - Display current simulation status (Running, Paused, Stopped)
   - Show elapsed time in "Day X, HH:MM UTC" format
   - Show current speed multiplier
   - Styled to integrate with existing header

3. **Modified: App.js**
   - Add simulation state management hooks
   - Modify data refresh logic to use dynamic intervals based on speed
   - Implement pause/resume logic
   - Implement reset functionality
   - Pass control handlers to SimulationControls component

4. **Modified: App.css**
   - Style SimulationControls component
   - Style SimulationStatusBar component
   - Ensure responsive design on all screen sizes
   - Add animations/transitions for state changes

## Implementation Details

### Refresh Rate Logic
- Base interval: 5000ms
- Effective interval = 5000 / simulationSpeed
- Apply pause by clearing/not setting the interval
- Resume by immediately calling refresh and resetting interval

### Elapsed Time Calculation
- Calculate elapsed milliseconds from simulation start
- Convert to simulated days and time: `Math.floor(elapsed / 86400000)` for days
- Format hours/minutes as HH:MM from remainder

### Button States
| State | Play | Pause | Stop | Speed Selector |
|-------|------|-------|------|----------------|
| Running | Disabled | Enabled | Enabled | Enabled |
| Paused | Enabled | Disabled | Enabled | Enabled |
| Stopped | Disabled | Disabled | Disabled | Enabled |

## UI Placement
- SimulationControls: Place in top header area, right side
- SimulationStatusBar: Place in top header area, center/right
- Ensure controls don't overlap with existing "Last Updated" display
- Mobile-responsive (stack on smaller screens if needed)

## Testing Considerations
- Verify speed changes work smoothly
- Test pause/resume preserves data
- Test reset clears all data properly
- Test elapsed time increments correctly
- Test button enable/disable states
- Test on mobile/tablet views
- Verify no memory leaks from interval management

🚨 ajv has ReDoS when using `$data` option

ajv (Another JSON Schema Validator) through version 8.17.1 is vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) when the $data option is enabled. The pattern keyword accepts runtime data via JSON Pointer syntax ($data reference), which is passed directly to the JavaScript RegExp() constructor without validation. An attacker can inject a malicious regex pattern (e.g., \"^(a|a)*$\") combined with crafted input to cause catastrophic backtracking. A 31-character payload causes approximately 44 seconds of CPU blocking, with each additional character doubling execution time. This enables complete denial of service with a single HTTP request against any API using ajv with $data: true for dynamic schema validation.

### Motivation

- Add a new Detective role and ability that can lock onto a target and be notified when that target uses abilities at night. 
- Allow certain observers (police/detective with an `Eavesdropping` passive) to receive copies of night private channel messages when they are watching a specific player. 
- Wire the new behavior into command handling and the night lifecycle so target selection and eavesdropping state are tracked and reset correctly.

### Description

- Add `DetectiveAbility` implementing `ActiveAbility` with activation, `resetNightState`, and `notifyTargetSelection` DM notification logic.

- Call `GameManager.relayNightPrivateChat` from the main message handler in `Main.kt`, and call `DetectiveAbility.notifyTargetSelection` from `AbilityUseCommand` when abilities target players.

ajv (Another JSON Schema Validator) through version 8.17.1 is vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) when the $data option is enabled. author: richmano-stack
body:
## Overview
This PR introduces the foundational server-authoritative multiplayer engine and matchmaking APIs for the typing game. It sets up the core infrastructure required to handle room creation, atomic joins utilizing Redis Lua scripting, and robust data schema validation.

## Changes Made
- **Multiplayer Mini SDK (`app/lib/multiplayer`)**:
  - `server-time.ts`: Added a helper to fetch consistent time directly from the Redis server to prevent client spoofing.
  - `parser.ts`: Implemented a parser to safely extract and validate Redis hash data, ensuring type safety for frontend consumption.
  - `lua.ts`: Added atomic Lua scripts (e.g., `JOIN_ROOM`) to handle complex state mutations like joining a room, preventing race conditions or over-filling lobbies.
  - `types.ts`: Defined strict TypeScript interfaces for our multiplayer state machine.

- **Matchmaking APIs (`app/api/race`)**:
  - `create/route.ts`: Implemented the endpoint to initialize a new game lobby in Redis (`WAITING_FOR_GUEST` state) with default fields and a 3600-second expiration TTL.
  - `join/route.ts`: Implemented the room joining logic which safely executes the `JOIN_ROOM` Lua script natively against Redis.

- **Bug Fixes**: 
  - Fixed a TypeScript module resolution issue (`Cannot find module`) where internal imports were failing due to a mismatch with how `tsconfig.json` configured the `@/*` alias. Updated faulty `@/app/lib/...` import paths to `@/lib/...`.

## Why these changes?
This structure firmly establishes our "Lazy Multiplayer" API polling approach. By pushing complex transactions—like state transitions and room capacity checks during `JOIN_ROOM`—to atomic Lua scripts running directly on Redis, we bypass the need for an always-on WebSocket server. This allows us to scale efficiently and stay within free-tier infrastructure limits without sacrificing data consistency.

author: lptr
body:
This PR consolidates the Ugly Duckling firmware from one binary per hardware generation (MK5, MK6, MK7, MK8, MKX)
down to one binary per chip platform (ESP32-S3 and ESP32-C6), using runtime MAC address detection to select the
correct device variant at boot.

This should reduce build times, and reduce complexity. This is especially important since we are to add a number of new generations soon as we mature the prototype hardware.

- **MAC-based device selection:** `macAddressMatchesAny()` (a variadic replacement for `macAddressStartsWith()`)
checks the device MAC against known prefixes at boot and calls the appropriate `startDevice<>` instantiation.
Unrecognized MACs abort with a clear error. A `UD_GEN` compile-time override is preserved for Wokwi simulation and
 local development.
- **Pins moved to instance members:** Each `DeviceDefinition` subclass now constructs its pins as member variables
 rather than global statics, so only the selected device's pins are ever registered.
- **`createBatteryDriver` made virtual:** Previously a static method called before the device object existed, it
is now a virtual instance method. `Device.hpp` instantiates the device first, then calls battery init through the
vtable.
- **MK6 hierarchy flattened:** `UglyDucklingMk6` (with internal revision detection) is replaced by
`UglyDucklingMk6Base` and three explicit subclasses (`Rev1`, `Rev2`, `Rev3`), each returning the correct
`motorNSleepPin()`. `Mk6Settings::motorNSleepPin` is removed.
- **MK8 hierarchy flattened:** `UglyDucklingMk8` is replaced by `UglyDucklingMk8Base` and two subclasses (`Rev1`
with INA219 omitted, `Rev2` with INA219 included). `Mk8Settings::disableIna219` is removed.
- **Build consolidation:** The CI matrix shrinks from 6 per-generation entries to 4 platform entries
(`esp32s3-release`, `esp32s3-debug`, `esp32c6-release`, `esp32c6-debug`), none of which set `UD_GEN`.
`DeviceCommon.cmake` now infers the platform from `IDF_TARGET` when `UD_GEN` is unset. The five per-generation
`sdkconfig.mk*.defaults` files are replaced by `sdkconfig.esp32s3.defaults` (16 MB flash) and
`sdkconfig.esp32c6.defaults` (8 MB flash).

## Notes

The MAC address ranges for MK5, MK6 Rev3, MK7, and MK8 Rev2 are currently **dummy placeholders** (marked with
`TODO` comments in `main.cpp`). These must be replaced with actual production ranges before the consolidated
binary is deployed to avoid the unrecognized-MAC abort path.

## Test plan

- [x] Build `esp32s3-release` and `esp32s3-debug` without `UD_GEN` — confirm clean compile for both
- [x] Build `esp32c6-release` and `esp32c6-debug` without `UD_GEN` — confirm clean compile for both
- [x] Build with `UD_GEN=MK6` — confirm Wokwi e2e test path still selects `UglyDucklingMk6Rev3`
- [x] Build with `UD_GEN=MK6_REV1` — confirm correct revision is selected
- [x] Verify CI matrix produces 4 artifacts named `ugly-duckling-esp32s3-release`, etc.
- [x] Flash an MK6 Rev1 device and confirm it boots correctly (MAC prefix `0x34:0x85:0x18` → Rev1 path)
- [x] Flash an MK8 Rev1 device and confirm INA219 is absent from the peripheral list
- [x] Flash an MK8 Rev2 device and confirm INA219 is present
- [x] Confirm unrecognized MAC aborts falls back to generic board definition

### Description
- Added a new abstraction `IFinalDexInspectionService` and implementation `FinalDexInspectionService` that opens the rebuilt/signed APK and scans `classes*.dex` entries for a literal method reference using `ContainsMethodReferenceAsync`.
- Updated `PatchPipelineService` to inject and use the final-inspection service, verify the patched activity reference `L<activity>;->loadFridaGadget()V` against the final artifact path (signed APK when signing is enabled), and emit a new `dex-verification` stage that fails with remediation guidance if the reference is missing.
- Wired the new service into DI in `App.axaml.cs` and added `ToClassDescriptor` helper for constructing the class descriptor string.
- Expanded `PatchPipelineServiceTests` to include the `dex-verification` stage in expected sequences, added a new test `RunAsync_ReturnsFailure_WhenInjectedMethodMissingInFinalDexArtifact`, and adjusted fakes to create/copy APK zip artifacts with `classes.dex` entries for realistic verification.

### Testing
- Updated unit tests in `tests/unit/PulseAPK.Tests/Services/Patching/PatchPipelineServiceTests.cs` to cover the new `dex-verification` stage and failure case when the final APK lacks the injected method reference.
- Attempted to run the pipeline tests with `dotnet test --filter PatchPipelineServiceTests`, but the test run could not be executed in this environment because `dotnet` is not installed (`/bin/bash: dotnet: command not found`).

body:
### Motivation
- Reduce redundant network requests and improve responsiveness when accessing material templates (`vorlagen`) by reusing cached data and preventing parallel fetches.
- Defer loading of `vorlagen` until the templates panel or material modal is actually opened to avoid unnecessary startup work.
- Ensure the UI can use a cached copy immediately while still updating from the server once.

### Description
- Introduce flags and a promise (`vorlagenCacheHydrated`, `vorlagenLoadedFromServer`, `vorlagenLoadingPromise`) to track cache hydration, server load state, and in-flight fetches in `loadVorlagen`.
- Make `loadVorlagen` return a promise and implement logic to serve cached templates first via `getVorlagenFromCache()`, skip repeated server requests when `vorlagenLoadedFromServer` is set, and reuse an ongoing fetch when `vorlagenLoadingPromise` is present.
- Persist server results with `saveVorlagenToCache()` and call `setVorlagen()` after loading, while ensuring `vorlagenLoadingPromise` is cleared in a `finally` block.
- Remove eager startup load and instead call `loadVorlagen()` lazily from `toggleVorlagenBereich()` and `openMaterialModal()` so templates are loaded when needed.

### Testing
- No automated tests were added or run as part of this change.

author: jabez-shekinah
body:
This pull request introduces a significantly improved user experience for setting up the SecureKit local agent. It adds automated setup scripts for both Windows and Mac/Linux, and revamps the frontend `AgentSetupPanel` to guide users through downloading, running, and connecting the agent—eliminating the need for manual command-line steps.

The most important changes are:

**Automated Setup Scripts**
* Added `StartAgent.bat` for Windows: Checks for Python and ngrok, installs dependencies, and launches both the agent and ngrok in separate windows for a seamless setup.
* Added `StartAgent.sh` for Mac/Linux: Checks for Python and ngrok, installs dependencies, and opens both the agent and ngrok in new terminals or background processes, with Homebrew support for ngrok installation.

**Frontend Usability & Workflow Improvements**
* Major overhaul of `AgentSetupPanel.tsx`:
  - Added download buttons for all required files and scripts, with clear step-by-step instructions for both Windows and Mac/Linux users.
  - Introduced an interactive Agent URL input panel, allowing users to paste their ngrok forwarding URL and connect without CLI commands. The UI detects ngrok URLs and provides reset functionality.
  - Updated UI copy and visuals to focus on ease of use, removing technical jargon and emphasizing a guided, code-free setup process.

**Dynamic URL Handling**
* All agent connection checks, status messages, and instructions now reference the user-configured agent URL instead of hardcoded localhost, ensuring accurate guidance regardless of setup. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d9a9ff22a6d61f468a5160f741722742964a00a6a6a8545677395b511e6c2405R231-L133) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d9a9ff22a6d61f468a5160f741722742964a00a6a6a8545677395b511e6c2405L144-R260) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d9a9ff22a6d61f468a5160f741722742964a00a6a6a8545677395b511e6c2405L61-R198)

These changes provide a much more accessible and user-friendly onboarding experience for SecureKit's local agent setup.

- Added AgentSetupPanel UI for agent configuration
- Implemented useLocalAgent hook for agent communication
- Added StartAgent.bat and StartAgent.sh for cross-platform setup
- Updated traffic analyzer to support local agent integration

### Motivation
- Provide a way to save "optional" places (backup sights / restaurants) per trip and surface them in the itinerary. 
- Allow users to export a trip summary and itinerary to a printable PDF from the Trip Overview. 
- Improve readability and consistency of itinerary, flight and hotel details with compact, reusable UI pieces.

### Description
- Add a new `OptionalStop` type and attach `optionalStops` to the `Trip` model, update `normTrip` to normalize incoming optional stop data and set initial `optionalStops` in `createTrip`.
- Add i18n keys for English and Chinese (`exportPdf`, `optionalPlaces`, `optionalPlacesDesc`, `addOptionalPlace`, `editOptionalPlace`, `saveOptionalPlace`, `noOptionalPlaces`, `noOptionalPlacesDesc`, `placeName`, `placeType`, `optionalLocation`, `reservationLink`, `optionalPlaceNotes`, `sight`, `restaurant`, `other`).
- Implement PDF export via `exportTripToPdf` (uses `escapeHtml`, `pdfList` and an iframe `srcdoc` + `print()` workflow) and wire it to a new button in the Trip Overview (`🧾 Export PDF`).
- Add optional-places UI to `TripItinerary`: toggleable tabs (`schedule` / `saved`), forms for adding/editing/removing optional stops, handlers (`saveOptionalStop`, `editOptionalStop`, `removeOptionalStop`), and persist via the existing trip update callback (prop `onTripUpdate`).
- Refactor small UI pieces: replace inline info rows with a styled `InfoRow` component, add `DetailHeader` for flight/hotel cards, and adjust paddings/typography across overview, itinerary and weather cards for improved layout.

author: geclos
body: ## Summary - replace broad web DB fallback behavior with a targeted runtime Postgres client repair path - when runtime auth fails (e.g. missing `latitude_app` role/grants in a fresh DB), automatically repair runtime role/user grants using the admin client and retry with the runtime client - add focused unit tests for runtime auth error detection, runtime client retry/repair behavior, and runtime role provisioning/grants - remove prior admin-fallback helper files in favor of runtime-repair modules - make runtime-role migration fail loudly if `latitude_app` is missing (remove optional `IF EXISTS` guard) ## Why Signing up with a brand-new account via magic link could fail on the first redirect to `/` with a 500 `RepositoryError` because web server functions use `LAT_DATABASE_URL` (runtime user), and in this environment the runtime role was missing/not granted. This change repairs runtime role access and enforces setup correctness by failing migration early if runtime role prerequisites are not met. ## Changes - `apps/web/src/server/clients.ts` - wire `getPostgresClient()` to a runtime client wrapper with repair callback - `apps/web/src/server/runtime-postgres-client.ts` - encapsulate runtime transaction retry-after-repair logic - `apps/web/src/server/runtime-postgres-role.ts` - parse runtime role/db from `LAT_DATABASE_URL` - ensure runtime role exists, set/update password, grant connect/schema/table/function/default privileges - execute repair using pg pool queries for compatibility in app/web package - tests: - `apps/web/src/server/runtime-postgres-client.test.ts` - `apps/web/src/server/runtime-postgres-role.test.ts` - removed obsolete files: - `apps/web/src/server/postgres-client-with-fallback.ts` - `apps/web/src/server/postgres-client-with-fallback.test.ts` - migration hardening: - `packages/platform/db-postgres/drizzle/20260310090909_setup-runtime-db-user/migration.sql` - removed `IF EXISTS` guard so grants fail loudly when `latitude_app` is absent ## Validation - targeted unit tests for new server modules - app/web typecheck - db-postgres package typecheck - manual signup -> magic-link -> first redirect verification with missing `latitude_app` role repro

body:
## Summary

This PR fixes two chat error-handling issues:

1. Invalid uploads from the empty chat state no longer create a new blank conversation.
2. First-message validation errors are now handled as expected results instead of bubbling up as redacted production Server Components errors.

## What changed

- made empty-state file uploads atomic by allowing `/api/upload` to work without a pre-created `conversationId`
- only create a conversation after file validation and parsing succeed
- returned `conversationId` from the upload response so the client can adopt the new draft conversation after a successful first upload
- added shared file preflight validation on the client while keeping server validation authoritative
- extracted shared first-message validation for the 1..4000 character rule
- changed `createConversation()` to return structured expected errors instead of throwing for validation/not-found cases
- updated empty-state conversation wiring to adopt uploaded conversations explicitly instead of creating them before upload
- centralized persisted custom UI message validation so both `data-agent-activity` and `data-uploaded-file` validate correctly on later sends

## Result

- uploading an invalid file from `/chat` shows the inline error and does not create a sidebar conversation
- valid first uploads still create/adopt the conversation correctly
- oversized first messages show a friendly validation error instead of the generic production redaction message
- persisted `data-agent-activity` parts continue to work across follow-up messages

- `pnpm build`

author: yeraze
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2364 — traceroutes showed "No response received" for nearby/fast-responding nodes despite the response being visible in logs and packet monitor.

### Root Cause

`recordTracerouteRequest()` for PostgreSQL/MySQL fired an **un-awaited async IIFE** to insert the pending traceroute record. For nearby nodes, the traceroute response arrived before the DB insert completed:

1. `sendTraceroute()` → sends packet, calls `await recordTracerouteRequestAsync()`
2. But the async wrapper called the inner method **without await** → returned immediately
3. Fast response arrives → `processTracerouteMessage()` runs
4. DB insert for the pending record is still in flight
5. Frontend reads stale DB state → shows "No response received"

### Fix

Made `recordTracerouteRequest()` properly async — removed the fire-and-forget IIFE and directly awaits the DB operations. The async wrapper now correctly awaits the inner method.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/services/database.ts` | Make `recordTracerouteRequest` async, remove un-awaited IIFE, await in async wrapper |

## Test plan

- [x] 3052 tests pass, 0 failures
- [x] SQLite path unchanged (already synchronous)
- [x] PostgreSQL/MySQL path now properly awaited

author: shoekstra
body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive implementation of the Toggl Track API v9 time entry management features in the Go client. It adds full support for listing, creating, updating, stopping, and deleting time entries, along with detailed usage documentation and improvements to the `TimeEntry` struct to better match the API.

**Time entry management features:**

* Implemented the `TimeEntriesService` in `time_entries.go`, providing methods for listing (`ListTimeEntries`), retrieving (`GetTimeEntry`, `GetRunningTimeEntry`), creating (`CreateTimeEntry`, `StartTimeEntry`), updating (`UpdateTimeEntry`), stopping (`StopTimeEntry`), and deleting (`DeleteTimeEntry`) time entries. Each method closely follows Toggl API v9 endpoints and supports relevant filtering and update options.
* Added option structs (`ListTimeEntriesOptions`, `CreateTimeEntryOptions`, `UpdateTimeEntryOptions`) for flexible API calls.
* Added a `patch` method to the `Client` in `request.go` to support PATCH requests required by the stop time entry endpoint.

**Data model improvements:**

* Updated the `TimeEntry` struct in `types.go` to match the Toggl API v9 response, including new fields such as `ProjectID`, `TaskID`, `ClientID`, `WorkspaceID`, `UserID`, `Billable`, `TagIDs`, `CreatedWith`, and `At`, and removed/renamed outdated fields.

**Documentation:**

* Expanded the `README.md` with installation instructions, a usage example, and an overview of available services, making it easier for users to get started with the library.

body:
## Summary
`@surfaice/action` — GitHub Action that checks for UI drift between committed `.surfaice.md` files and the live app.

## What It Does
1. Reads committed `.surfaice.md` files from `surfaice-dir`
2. Fetches each route from the live app with `Accept: text/surfaice`
3. Diffs committed vs live using `@surfaice/differ`
4. Reports drift and fails the action if `fail-on-drift: true`

## Files
- `packages/action/action.yml`: Action definition (inputs/outputs)
- `packages/action/src/index.ts`: Node 20 runner entry point
- `packages/action/README.md`: Usage docs
- `examples/github-action/ui-drift.yml`: Ready-to-copy workflow

## Usage
```yaml
- uses: surfaiceai/surfaice/packages/action@main
  with:
    base-url: 'http://localhost:3000'
    surfaice-dir: 'surfaice/'
    fail-on-drift: 'true'
```

body:
## Summary

Add a shared `fetchWithRetry` helper in `steam-api.ts` that applies timeout and bounded retry handling to all Steam API requests. This is the foundational infrastructure fix that unblocks 8 downstream issues.

## Changes

- **`src/steam-api.ts`** — Added exported `fetchWithRetry` helper:
  - 15s timeout via `AbortSignal.timeout()` per request
  - Exponential backoff retry on transient failures (429, 5xx, network errors, timeouts)
  - No retry on 4xx auth/privacy/validation failures
  - `Retry-After` header support on 429 (capped at 30s)
  - Signal composition via `AbortSignal.any()` (preserves caller abort signals)
  - Response body cleanup before retry (`res.body?.cancel()`)
  - All 10 bare `fetch()` calls migrated to use the helper

- **`src/steam-api.test.ts`** — 11 new tests covering:
  - Timeout behavior
  - Retry on 5xx, 429, network errors, timeouts
  - Max retries exhausted
  - Retry-After header respect
  - Non-retryable error passthrough
  - Updated 5 existing assertions for new fetch call signature

## Verification

- Typecheck: ✅ clean
- Lint: ✅ clean  
- Tests: ✅ 27 passed (up from 16 baseline)
- Adversarial code review (GPT-5.3-Codex): 2 findings fixed before commit

## Acceptance Criteria (from #3)

- [x] All network requests use a shared helper
- [x] Requests time out after a bounded interval (15s)
- [x] Retries are limited (max 2) and only apply to transient failures
- [x] Existing callers still receive meaningful error messages
- [x] Tests cover timeout and retry behavior

Closes #3
